Create a study project with `uv`, then add SCGSim from the current `develop` branch. SCGSim supports Python `>=3.12,<3.14`.

## 1. Install uv and Git

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads). Git lets `uv` fetch SCGSim from the [canonical source repository](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim).

Check: `uv --version` and `git --version` each print an installed version.

## 2. Create the project and add SCGSim

Initialize a project with Python 3.12 and add SCGSim from `develop`:

```bash
uv init --bare --python 3.12 scgsim-study
cd scgsim-study
uv add 'scgsim @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git' --branch develop
```

`uv.lock` records the exact Git revision selected when the dependency is resolved.

## 3. Check the installation

Run a Python import and print the installed package version:

```bash
uv run python -c 'import scgsim; from importlib.metadata import version; print(version("scgsim"))'
```

Check: the command prints the installed SCGSim version without an import error.

## Add a backend extra

The base package reads returned results. To prepare Palace runs, add an extra to the existing SCGSim dependency:

```bash
uv add --extra palace scgsim
```

Use `aedt`, `aedt-epr`, or `visualization` when you need those features. The extra is added to the existing Git dependency and keeps its configured source.

## Rebuild the environment on another computer

Keep `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` with the study. On another computer, run `uv sync` in the project directory to recreate the locked environment:

```bash
uv sync
```
